Subject: Capacity add + MSA redline - initial ask

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed with the throughput numbers. We
are preparing an internal memo to expand our committed capacity and need to align the
contract language before we proceed. Two asks: 1) can you confirm a short lead time for a
+30% capacity top-up on our current order form; and 2) attached is our legal team's redline
of the MSA (EdgeHealth_MSA_redline_20260810.docx).

Major concern from our security team: a clause about log retention and audit access that
we marked as "required". Also the SOW needs a small clarification about the test data
segregation process. We prefer to keep changes minimal — customer success is ready to
onboard the expanded workload next month pending legal sign-off.

Can we get an internal point of contact from Redwood legal to review the MSA redline this
week? We have a DocuSign window the week of Aug 17.

Thanks,
Tom Reyes

procurement@edgehealth.com

Hi Tom — thanks for the redline, and congrats on the quick internal alignment.

Looping in Jonas (Legal) and Laura (Account Exec) to coordinate. Quick responses to your
asks: 1) +30% top-up is operationally doable within our standard provisioning SLA (48–72
hours) once an order form is fully executed; 2) we will review the MSA redline and come back
with proposed edits that preserve our encryption/audit posture.

Jonas — can you prioritize a pass on the MSA and the SOW note about test-data segregation?
If you need a short call with EdgeHealth legal, Laura can help schedule.

Tom — we plan to provide a change order draft + proposed counter-redline by EOD Tue (Aug

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity add + MSA redline - initial ask

Hi all,

I've completed an initial pass on the MSA redline and attached a focused counter-redline
(package: EdgeHealth_MSA_redline_20260810.docx - reviewed). Summary of changes we
intend to propose:

- Retain Redwood's standard log-retention limits but accept a scoping carve-out for
  "audit-ready extracts" (48-hour turnaround) rather than full continuous external access.
- Clarify that test data segregation will be implemented at the tenant level with
  documented separation and ephemeral test environments, noted in SOW exhibit B.
- Limit the indemnity expansion suggested by EdgeHealth; propose a mutual cap tied to
  the order form fees (see clause 12).

Jonas (internal note): I flagged the proposed "on-prem audit kiosks" language — not
compatible with our hosted proposition; recommend the customer use a redacted extract
process instead.

Tom — would EdgeHealth accept a 48-hour SLA for audit extracts plus a scheduled monthly
"audit package" delivery to their security team? That avoids kiosk-style access while giving
regular observability.

Attachment: OrderForm-EdgeHealth-Aug2026.pdf; SOW_v3_EdgeHealth.docx

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

From: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@edgehealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Sana Patel <sana.patel@edgehealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 13:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity add + MSA redline - initial ask

Thanks Jonas — that summary helps. We discussed internally and EdgeHealth is willing to
accept the 48-hour "audit extract" approach as long as the monthly audit package includes
full request traces for the sample window and a signed attestation by Redwood's security
ops. Our security lead (Sana) would like the attestation language included in the SOW.

Two follow-ups: 1) can the SOW exhibit B include a short paragraph on the attestation
content; and 2) Laura, can you share the change order with updated fees (we're expecting
a prorated credit for current unused capacity when the top-up takes effect).

If we can get the updated Order Form + SOW exhibit by Wed EOD (Aug 12) we can keep the
DocuSign slot for that week.

Tom
